doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: Tom Anderson, Basin Street cabarets and policemen in cabarets
summary: Tom Anderson's cabaret, Josie Arlington, and the policeman kept in every cabaret.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: did you know Tom Anderson what you mean the boss yeah who was he I want to get that straight
he was a big man who was a politician and he had everything to say I knew him I only saw him yeah because I worked as I say only one door away from him and I worked in the black cat for about a
year oh the black cat was next door on ramp on the same two doors yeah only one door in between where was the Arlington annex now I don't know

the Arlington Josie Josie Josie Arlington that was on Basin Street what's his name ought to be Josie Arlington that was on Basin Street that was Tom Anderson had a place right on the corner Tom Anderson had the real class cabaret in those days see right on the corner and then down on the same side of the street was uh Arlington and Lulu White see he used to have colored help

and I'll never forget I used to go in there for my fried ham you know and fried potatoes and that that was a nightly affair I also never forget the fella's name that ran the black cat it was called Bull Riley was the sheriff you know those days you had a big job you were put in charge of a cabaret so nobody would bother you I'll tell you a good idea they had in those days they had a policeman in every cabaret you remember Buck there never were any fights there were never any because uh what a uniform cop sitting there nobody's gonna start it isn't like it is you know like some of these places today where they come in there looking for trouble every every place had a cop had to pay him you know and I thought there was a very good idea and they ought to put it in effect and the places I was at the other night they could stand two uniformed cops with some of the people that's a fact that's where

they run me off the street the other night I had to get off it was so bad you know I had to sit right under the bandstand what about uh the tuxedo dance at all two and a half a night on Franklin street did you ever go there you mean the tuxedo in the district in those days all the cabarets well that was uh like all the rest of them it was just one of them had cop in
